Key Takeaways

Reddit shares fell 5% on Monday as worries about slowing growth weighed on the stock ahead of its third-quarter report on Oct. 29.

The fourth-quarter outlook matters more than the third-quarter beat, because it shows whether growth is slowing as gradually as analysts expect.

At 16x forward earnings, Reddit trades at the bottom of its one-year range, though analysts have raised their 2027 earnings estimate by 25% since the end of 2025.

Watch for a fourth-quarter revenue guide of about $1.05 billion and for U.S. daily users above the second quarter's 53.2 million.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) fell 5% on Monday as worries about slowing growth hung over its third-quarter report, due after the close on Thursday, Oct. 29. Snap fell 3% the same day and Meta barely moved, so the selling hit Reddit's own growth story hardest.

Reddit has beaten the top of its own revenue guidance by $58 million to $80 million in each of the last three quarters. Another third-quarter beat wouldn't surprise anyone. The fourth-quarter outlook is the number that decides whether the stock's multiple holds.

The slowdown is already in the guidance

When Reddit reported in July, it guided third-quarter revenue to $860 million to $870 million, up 47% to 49%. That's a step down from the second quarter, when revenue grew 61% to $805 million.

It also stopped reporting U.S. logged-in daily users as a separate number, after that figure grew just 1% in the second quarter, to 23.1 million.

Analysts expect the slowdown to keep going. Consensus calls for revenue of $3.39 billion in 2026, up 54% from 2025's $2.2 billion, then $4.47 billion in 2027 (up 32%) and $5.58 billion in 2028 (up 25%).

Reddit (RDDT): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024–2028 (TIKR)

To hit that 2026 figure, Reddit needs fourth-quarter revenue of roughly $1.05 billion to $1.06 billion, up about 45% from last year's $726 million. A guide in that range keeps the analysts' path intact. A guide below it would push analysts to cut their numbers, unless investors trust Reddit to beat its guide again the way it has all year.

The multiple already prices in a steeper slowdown

Even after Monday's drop, Reddit trades at 16x forward earnings. That's the lowest point of the past year, against an average of 26x and a high of 49x in mid-January.

Reddit Sinks 9% Into Q3 Report as U.S. User Growth Slows to 6% ©Brett Jordan from Pexels and creatoroflove via Canva
Key Takeaways

Reddit fell 9.2% over the past week to $137 ahead of its October 29 third-quarter report.

Second-quarter revenue rose 61% to $805 million, but third-quarter guidance implies growth slowing to 47% to 49%.

U.S. daily active uniques grew just 6% while international users jumped 28%, shifting growth toward markets that monetize at lower rates.

At 16.0x forward earnings with about $2.8 billion in net cash, the stock already prices in real doubt.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) heads into Thursday's third-quarter report with an awkward split screen. The business just logged its eighth straight quarter of growth above 60%.

Yet the stock closed at $137 on October 27, down 9.2% over the past week. It now sits 48% below its 52-week high of $264.

The gap says investors are pricing in a slowdown, and management has already confirmed one. Third-quarter guidance calls for growth of 47% to 49%.

That is still enormous for a company this size. But a stock that joined the S&P 500 in August on momentum tends to trade on the rate of change, so October 29 is about the slope.

Growth is cooling from a high base

Second-quarter numbers left little to criticize. Revenue rose 61% to $805 million, well ahead of the $730 million consensus.

Advertising revenue grew 64% to $762 million.

Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $343 million, a 43% margin.

Diluted EPS climbed to $1.25 from $0.45.

The third-quarter guide calls for $860 million to $870 million in revenue and $385 million to $395 million in adjusted EBITDA. Both topped consensus, yet the midpoint still marks a clear step down from 61%.

Here is how that curve has bent across recent quarters:

Reddit (RDDT): total revenue, quarterly, $ millions, Q2 2024–Q2 2026 (TIKR)

Reddit added more than $500 million of quarterly revenue in two years. So each new point of growth now requires a much larger dollar gain.

International users carry the load

Daily active uniques rose 18% to 130.3 million. The mix is the real story.

International DAUq jumped 28% to 77.1 million while the U.S. grew only 6% to 53.2 million. The higher-monetizing U.S. audience is maturing, and growth is shifting to markets that earn less per user.

Management's long-term framework targets 1 billion global users and 100 million in the U.S. It also says new-user retention improved 50% year over year, which it treats as its main signal of product quality.

Does Wall Street still believe in a steep path from here?

Reddit (RDDT): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023–2028 (TIKR)

Consensus implies roughly 42.5% annual revenue growth over the next two years. That only works if international users monetize faster and data licensing, which lifted other revenue 24% to $43 million, keeps expanding.

Factors Likely to Have Influenced Q3 Performance

Reddit's third-quarter 2026 performance is expected to have benefited from robust advertising demand, expanding advertiser adoption and continued investments in artificial intelligence (AI)-powered advertising solutions. In the second quarter, advertising revenues surged 64% year over year to $762 million, supported by higher impressions and pricing. Active advertisers increased more than 70%, while revenues from the scaled channel, comprising mid-market businesses and small and mid-sized businesses, doubled year over year. These trends are expected to have continued into the third quarter as well.

The company is expected to have benefited from increasing adoption of Reddit Max, its AI-powered advertising automation platform, in the to-be-reported quarter. In the second quarter of 2026, the number of advertisers using Reddit Max rose more than 60% sequentially, while revenues generated from Max campaigns surged more than 150%. The introduction of tailored creatives and app-install optimization capabilities is likely to have improved advertising efficiency, enhanced campaign performance and encouraged higher advertiser spending.

Improving user engagement and international monetization are also expected to have supported growth. In the second quarter of 2026, the platform reached more than 500 million weekly users and exceeded 130 million daily users. New app user retention improved 50% year over year on a relative basis. Enhanced feed recommendation models, improved onboarding experiences and higher conversion of web visitors into app users are expected to have supported engagement and advertising monetization. International revenues surged 84% year over year in the second quarter, indicating significant growth potential.

However, Reddit's third-quarter 2026 results are expected to have been hurt by volatility in search referral traffic, particularly amid the growing adoption of AI-powered search summaries, which could have weighed on user growth and engagement. Higher investments in AI, machine learning, product development and marketing are likely to have increased operating expenses.

title: Reddit vs. Snap: Which Social Media Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Reddit vs. Snap: Which Social Media Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Robert Izquierdo, The Motley Fool
Tue, October 27, 2026 at 2:28 AM EDT 6 min read
RDDT
SNAP
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

As digital communities and visual communication evolve, investors are weighing the merits of different social platforms. Should you put your capital behind Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) or Snap (NYSE:SNAP) in 2026?

Reddit operates a community-driven platform built on niche interests and deep archives, while Snap focuses on ephemeral messaging for younger demographics. Both companies compete for digital advertising dollars against much larger rivals. Here is a comparison of their financials, user growth, and valuation to see which fits better in a diversified portfolio of investing in social media stocks.

The case for Reddit

Reddit operates a massive community platform where users create topic-based discussions and exchange insights. The company generates the majority of its revenue through third-party advertising, which accounted for approximately 94% of revenue in 2025. Customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business, as the top ten largest advertisers account for roughly 21% of total revenue. Reddit is also exploring a content licensing model where it sells data to companies training generative artificial intelligence models.

In its 2025 fiscal year (FY), revenue reached $2.2 billion, representing a year-over-year increase of 69.4%. The company reported net income of $529.7 million during this period. This resulted in a net margin of 24.1%, which is a significant improvement over the net loss reported in the prior fiscal year. High growth and positive earnings suggest the platform is successfully scaling its ad business.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company carried a debt-to-equity ratio of zero, indicating it has no total debt relative to its shareholder equity. Its current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations with current assets, was 11.6x. Free cash flow for the year was $684.2 million. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented 49.7% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Snap

Snap is a technology company focused on its Snapchat camera application and various augmented reality services. It derives a substantial majority of its revenue from third-party advertising, which accounted for 87% of total revenue in FY 2025. While advertising remains the primary driver, the company has successfully introduced Snapchat+, a subscription model with more than 25 million subscribers. Snap works with a broad range of advertisers from small businesses to global brands.

title: 3 Reasons to Buy Reddit Stock This Week
detail:
3 Reasons to Buy Reddit Stock This Week
Rick Munarriz, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 8:23 AM EDT 5 min read
RDDT
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

It's showtime for Reddit (NYSE: RDDT) and its investors. Shares of the company behind the popular online forum with more than half a billion users reports its third-quarter results after Thursday's market close.

Expectations are high. The stock price is low. There are some pretty good reasons to be hopeful for a big bounce on Friday, but hold your optimism in check. There are still some serious red flags waving in the wind. Still, I think it's good to warm up to the "community of communities" platform operator. Let's break down the reasons it could be a good buy this week ahead of its telltale financials.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
1. Reddit is historically cheap

Reddit stock has gone cold after a pair of monster rallies since going public in early 2024. The shares are trading 37% lower in 2027, down nearly half from their peak 13 months ago.

A stock doesn't slide in a vacuum. There are some potential potholes to watch for -- and I will get there, eventually -- but few things excite me as much as a stock that's sliding despite strong fundamentals. Reddit's business is booming.

Revenue soared 61% in Reddit's latest quarter, its eighth consecutive quarter of better than 60% top-line growth. Earnings, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), and free cash flow more than doubled. You would think that the price of admission for this high-octane performance would be a healthy market premium. Spoiler alert: Reddit is cheaper than you think.

RDDT data: YCharts.

Reddit is now trading for almost 20 times next year's earnings, but less than 15 times the bottom-line target for 2028. This is near a historical low for Reddit, admittedly, given its short time as a public company. Growth should slow from here, but shouldn't a company posting this kind of growth be worth a healthy premium to the market?

2. Reddit is an earnings season beast

Reddit has now gone through 10 earnings seasons as a publicly traded company. It has consistently topped Wall Street revenue and profit targets. But that doesn't mean stretching that winning streak to 11 will send the shares higher.

Reddit stock has fallen the day after reporting quarterly results in roughly half of its updates. Sometimes there are valuation concerns. With that off the table now, the deal-breaker has been a lack of long-term visibility.
